sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader for the State and perused the material available on record.

2. This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C seeking anticipatory bail in Crime No.166/2022 registered at Garag police station, for offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 323, 498A, 504,
506 and 149 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
3. Complaint is lodged by the wife of petitioner No.1/accused No.1.
The gist of the complaint averments are that the marriage of the complainant with petitioner No.1 was performed on 25.12.2020 as per Hindu rituals.
After her marriage, she lived in the matrimonial home happily for about one month.
From 20.02.2021, her husband and in-laws started quarrelling with her, doubting her character and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and demanded to bring 50 grams of gold as dowry.

In the month of June, when she was two and half month pregnant, they abused her stating that the baby in the womb does not belong to accused No.1 and assaulted and kicked her on her stomach, on account of which she suffered miscarriage.
Her mother took her to her house on 27.06.2022 and the petitioners threatened her not to return to their house without bringing gold and also instigated her to commit suicide.
Further, on 12.08.2022 at about 6 p.m., when she was in her parental home, her husband came and abused her in filthy language and threatened her etc.

4. Petitioner No.1 is the husband of complainant, petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the parents, petitioner Nos.4, 6 and 7 are the brothers of petitioner No.1 and petitioner No.5 is the wife of petitioner No.4.
5. As per the complaint averments, marriage of the complainant with petitioner No.1 took place on 25.12.2020.

It is alleged that only for about one month, complainant was looked after properly in her matrimonial home and thereafter her husband and other relatives subjected her to physical and mental cruelty etc. and they demanded her to bring 50 grams of gold from her parental house.
It is alleged that on 24.06.2022, at about 8 a.m. she was assaulted and kicked by the accused persons on her stomach due to which she suffered miscarriage.
It is also alleged that complainant's mother took her back to their house on 27.06.2022 and since then she is residing in her parental home.

On 12.08.2022, at about 6 p.m. her husband i.e. petitioner No.1 is alleged to have gone to her parental home and abused her in filthy language and threatened her etc.
6.
An omnibus allegations are made against accused Nos.2 to 7 that all of them were giving physical and mental torture etc.
Except the self serving statement, at this stage there is no material to substantiate the allegations.
There is no material to show that the complainant suffered miscarriage and it was on account of assault by the accused persons.

However, there is specific allegation against her husband i.e. petitioner No.1 that he used to burn her with mosquito sticks and also smash her bangles and cause injuries to her with the broken bangles etc.
7.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, relief sought by petitioner Nos.2 to 7 can be granted.
However, petitioner No.1 is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

Hence, the following:

sentences.text:
In the event of arrest of petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 7 in Crime No.166/2022 of Garag Police Station, they shall be released, subject to following conditions:
1) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 7 shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of 10 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) each with two sureties for likesum.
2) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 7 shall make themselves available for the purpose of investigation and they shall co-operate with the investigation.
3) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 7 shall furnish their residential address proof and shall inform the Investigation Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
4) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 7 shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
5) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 7 shall not indulge in any criminal activities.
6) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 7 shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.

Sd/-
